Volkswagen Beetle Returns Once Again, This Time as an ID. Series Model in Hot Hatchback CGI Form
8 photos
Photo: augusto_fuchsdesign / Instagram
The Volkswagen Beetle is probably one of the most important automobiles of all time, especially the original series which ran from 1938 until 2003 for no less than 65 years. It’s really no wonder that Volkswagen tried to continue in its spirit with two modern incarnations, right?
Officially known as the Volkswagen Type 1 , the Beetle was a small family car with a distinctive bug-like design, which over the years brought it universal recognition and numerous nicknames, plus over 21.5 million sales. Since it was only offered as a single generation, the production time of 65 years even today stands as a record, by the way.
Volkswagen tried to recapture its popularity and colloquial spirit with the Volkswagen New Beetle produced from 1997 through 2011 and then again made another attempt with the A5 version until 2019. It wasn’t meant to be, as none of these versions achieved the success of their illustrious predecessor, and VW decided to stop trying to offer a retro model akin to the likes of the MINI Cooper, for example.
On the other hand, nowadays it seems there’s a growing roster of EV hot hatchbacks around the world, including the newly released Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI, but also the likes of the Hyundai Ioniq 5 N, MINI John Cooper Works Electric, Abarth 500e and 600e, plus the Alpine A290, which is based on the retro-modern Renault 5 E-Tech.
As such, it’s really no wonder that someone thought about this niche for a potential fourth outing of the iconic Volkswagen Beetle – and since that person is a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators, they also did something about it rather than just dwelling aimlessly across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI.
Meet Augusto Fuchs, aka ' augusto_fuchsdesign ' on social media, who is a Transportation Design Master at IED Torino and Surface Modeler & Designer for Airbus Helicopters, and their most recent unofficial, hypothetical design project: the VW ID. Beetle Beast. It should be a part of the novel ID. series, which includes novelties like the Volkswagen ID. Polo, Cross, and Tiguan , but it would obviously act as the hero model tasked with bringing enthusiasts to the brand.
The credentials are unchanged for the modern revival – it’s still a bug-like model with a distinctive silhouette and signature round headlights, but now it would probably make not just the small EV hot hatchbacks feel uncomfortable next to it but also frighten the larger models like the popular Hyundai Ioniq 5 N.
It’s also clearly a specialist car, with room for just four on board due to the arching roofline and packing all the aerodynamic goodies of the late 2020s, including a widebody kit and massive aero elements like the front splitters and the humongous diffuser plus wing around the back.
